title: Decide how data persists
subtitle: Choose a simple design and know its limits.
concept: Storage design depends on readers and writers, retention, recovery and future format changes.
intuition: Notes on one computer and a shared cloud document have different access, recovery and collaboration behavior.
objectives: Specify fields, types, unique identity and allowed input.
Practice valid restoration and invalid rejection; handle format versions explicitly.

body.title: Give records a clear shape
body.text: Each record has id, title and done: identity, readable text and completion state. Backups wrap tasks in a versioned object. Versions identify formats. Duplicate titles are allowed; IDs must be unique. These contracts affect creation, display, deletion, tests and restoration, so renaming one field in isolation is unsafe.

body.title: Local storage can fail
body.text: localStorage stores strings for an origin across page loads. Users can clear it; browsers may restrict or reject writes; capacity is limited. Tabs may overwrite one another, and this example has no concurrency coordination. It suits a personal first release, not a reliable multiuser database.

body.title: A backup matters only if it restores
body.text: Export JSON and actually restore it. Reject bad data without replacing existing records. Report failed writes. If reading fails, pause writes rather than overwriting damaged data with an empty list. Recognize versions and migrate or reject explicitly. This example implements no complex migration and rejects versions other than 1.

formalDefinition.text: Storage design depends on readers and writers, retention, recovery and future format changes.
conditions: For small personal learning projects. In shared repositories, follow the team's conventions.
This method produces checkable evidence; it cannot guarantee arbitrary AI output is correct.

workflow: Specify fields, types, unique identity and allowed input.
Explain data location, retention and failure cases.

workedExamples.title: Why titles are not IDs
workedExamples.problem: Two plans are titled Practice Git. How can only the second be completed?
steps: Pass the chosen ID from the interface action.
Locate by ID instead of matching every title.
workedExamples.answer: Titles support reading; IDs locate records. Same-title items can have different completion states, giving identity a practical purpose.

workedExamples.title: Why version backups?
workedExamples.problem: A new backup replaces done with status. Can the old program read it?
steps: The current program expects boolean done.
An unknown format may render incorrectly.
Recognize the version and deliberately migrate or reject.
workedExamples.answer: The program accepts only version: 1 with id/title/done. Reject unknown versions while preserving the list. Future upgrades need explicit migration rules and tests, not assumed compatibility.

commonMistakes.claim: Local saving means data cannot be lost.
commonMistakes.correction: Clearing, storage errors, changed devices and changed origins can remove access. Keep restorable backups.

commonMistakes.claim: A download button proves backups are reliable.
commonMistakes.correction: Download a valid file and restore its complete content and state.

practice.answer: id: nonempty unique string; title: 1–80 code units after trimming; done: boolean.

practice.problem: Do localhost and 127.0.0.1 share data on the same port?
practice.answer: No. Protocol, host and port jointly determine localStorage origin.
solution: One computer does not imply one storage space.
Use backup restoration to migrate instead of assuming it happens.

practice.problem: Why avoid writing an empty list after a damaged read?
practice.answer: That overwrites old content. Pause writes, explain the failure and restore deliberately from a valid backup.
solution: A read failure does not mean the user had no data.

practice.problem: Can the first release handle concurrent multiuser editing unchanged?
practice.hint: It lacks shared storage, permissions and conflict coordination.
practice.answer: No. Reconfirm requirements and design shared storage, identity, permissions and conflicts.
solution: Changing domains or adding a button is insufficient.

learningCheck.question: Why use IDs rather than titles alone?
choices: To target one of several same-title records
feedback: Titles may repeat; IDs distinguish records.
IDs do not provide shared storage.

steps.question: Reading the current list fails.
choices: Pause writes, preserve old data and explain

steps.question: A backup has an unknown version.
choices: Reject explicitly until migration is designed
Ignore the version and load anyway
Assume every done value is true
feedback: The format may differ and loading can corrupt records.

steps.question: What should a restoration rehearsal inspect?
choices: Every ID, title and completion state
feedback: Complete records support the restoration conclusion.
Size does not establish correct meaning.
